title: Meta’s new One subscriptions put a price on social media and AI
content:
Shortly after launching its new do-everything AI assistant Muse, Meta’s launching subscription bundles that pair its standalone app subscriptions with extra AI usage. Some of the new Meta One bundles were in testing earlier this year, but are now available globally starting today, with several tiers for individual users, creators, and businesses. Meta says the “core experience” on its apps and Meta AI will still be free, and users can still get its subscriptions for Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp without a bundle. It also says it plans to expand the bundles to include “Edits, AI glasses, and more over time.”
Meta’s new One subscriptions put a price on social media and AI
Meta One bundles start at $7.99 per month with perks like 48-hour Instagram stories and a bold follow button.
There are two bundles for individual users, Core for $7.99 per month and Premium for $19.99 per month. They include Instagram Plus, WhatsApp Plus, and Facebook Plus, with “more media generation with Meta AI,” like generating images with Muse or using in-app AI features like Instagram’s Restyle. That’s a few dollars cheaper than paying $11 per month for all three of the standalone subscriptions.
The Meta One subscriptions aimed at creators and businesses range from $14.99 to $499 per month. They also include Meta’s individual app subscriptions, along with perks like a bold follow button, a verified badge, higher rankings in search results, and monitoring for fake impersonation accounts:
- Essential ($14.99/month): Establish yourself and build confidence with new audiences. Get tools to manage your presence and more access to Meta Business Agent on WhatsApp to respond to customers 24/7. Plus, a verified badge, verified channel on WhatsApp Business app, and impersonation protection so people know you’re who you say you are (pending successful verification).
- Advanced ($49.99/month): Invest in professional-grade tools. Advanced publishing features like scheduling stories up to 30 days in advance, links in organic posts and reels, exportable analytics, and deeper audience insights. Give team members access to your account without sharing your password and get more linked devices and business broadcast credits on WhatsApp. Plus, even more Meta Business Agent responses.
- Expert ($149/month) and Max ($499/month): Scale and optimize. These plans include our highest levels of feature access and Meta Business Agent capacity for teams managing at scale.

report.summary: Meta launches Meta One subscription bundles globally, combining Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp perks with extra Meta AI/Muse usage, starting at $7.99/month.
report.background: Meta has long relied on advertising to keep Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp free. But AI features are expensive to run, and ad growth is maturing, so the company is testing consumer and business subscriptions. After launching its Muse AI assistant, Meta is bundling app perks with extra AI usage. This follows a broader industry shift: OpenAI, Microsoft, Google, and others sell premium AI tiers, while social platforms add paid creator and business tools. Meta previously tested some Meta One bundles earlier this year. The move signals that 'free' social media may remain, but advanced AI, creator reach, and business automation are becoming paid upgrades. It also positions Meta against rivals in both social and AI subscription markets.
key_points: Meta One individual bundles include Core at $7.99/month and Premium at $19.99/month. They bundle Instagram Plus, WhatsApp Plus, and Facebook Plus with extra Meta AI usage, such as generating images with Muse or using Instagram Restyle. Meta says this is a few dollars cheaper than paying $11/month for the three standalone subscriptions.

Creator and business tiers range from $14.99 to $499/month. Essential adds verification and impersonation protection; Advanced adds scheduling, links, analytics, and team access; Expert and Max offer higher limits and more Meta Business Agent capacity for teams managing at scale.

The core Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Meta AI experiences remain free, and users can still buy standalone app subscriptions. Meta plans to expand Meta One bundles over time to include Edits, AI glasses, and more services.

The launch follows Muse, Meta's do-everything AI assistant, and shows Meta monetizing AI directly. Bundling social perks with AI usage creates an upsell ladder, increases lock-in, and tests willingness to pay for features that were historically free.

Meta is joining a wider subscription race in tech. X, Snap, and others sell premium social tiers, while OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft charge for advanced AI. Meta One blends both trends into one global bundle for individuals, creators, and businesses.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Meta One validates bundling AI with existing consumer services, pressuring rivals to combine assistants, social features, and business automation. Developers may see more demand for agentic tools and integrations, but also more closed, metered ecosystems. Creators and businesses face new costs for visibility, verification, analytics, and AI customer support, potentially widening the gap between free and paying users. Regular users keep free access, but the best AI generation, reach, and protections move behind paywalls. If successful, Meta One could normalize subscriptions across social media, making 'free' platforms increasingly tiered and ad-plus-subscription hybrid models standard.
report.tools: To follow this shift, watch Meta AI/Muse, Instagram Restyle, and WhatsApp Business Agent. Compare with ChatGPT Plus, Google Gemini Advanced, and Anthropic Claude Pro. Creators can try Buffer, Later, Hootsuite, or Metricool for scheduling and analytics. Open-source alternatives include Meta's Llama models, Mistral, Stable Diffusion, and ComfyUI for image generation. These help assess whether Meta One's bundled value beats standalone AI and social management tools.
